scope: Exploratory continuation after the finite-list physical-pair method; freeze this comparison before executing it
revision: run_02 adds the loading-controlled curvature remainder and whole-cell time-varying joint predictor. Original run_01 sources/results preserved. Candidate lists, observation information, tolerances, pointwise solver budget and previous variants unchanged.
comparison_contract: All variants share v1 phase/input-floor/physical-pair gates, exact kernels, full-tail envelopes, solver fallback, pointwise mesh budget and tolerances. Only reuse across target times changes. Shared numerical cache is charged separately to each workflow; no wall-clock speed claim.
go_criteria: Record gains AND losses relative to every resolved v1 candidate, not only aggregate sufficient counts
Check every sufficient returned joint estimate at nominal and both endpoint input scalings
Check whole-time-cell guarantees at additional interior physical times, not only listed candidates
Report work at both candidate densities and the convex-secant ablation
Do not conflate continuous covered subintervals with a continuum earliest prediction time
limitations: Same four deterministic synthetic spectra and 12 observation sets; densities and input envelopes reuse information
Known positive polynomial loading histories, deterministic bands, zero prehistory, no common mass/rate caps
The upper endpoint is convex and both endpoints decrease; no monotonicity or convexity of the diameter is assumed
Empty transported inner overlap is a missing lower witness, not an infeasibility result
No extrapolation outside two computed bounded target times
Positive input-envelope scaling is inherited from the earlier exact reduction
Failure remains unresolved; floating-point replay is not directed rounding or external review
A fixed candidate search can cover continuous subintervals but does not prove a global earliest time
The test does not establish improved physical point-prediction accuracy or real-material validity
